title: Bagdad: How a Shelby County Rail Stop Took Over Consolation
summary: Bagdad in northeastern Shelby County grew after the Louisville and Frankfort Railroad arrived about 1850, pulling settlers a mile west from Consolation.
bodyMarkdown:
Bagdad, in northeastern Shelby County, is a town the railroad moved. Before the tracks came, families in this corner of the county gathered at a crossroads called Consolation, which had its own post office from 1849. It was farm country, rolling and well watered, a half day's ride from Frankfort and a longer haul to Louisville.

About 1850 the Louisville and Frankfort Railroad built its line across the area. The new road gave farmers a way to ship goods east to the capital and west to the river market at Louisville without a slow wagon trip. A depot went up about a mile west of Consolation, and a mill followed beside the tracks. Stores and houses drifted toward the station, and Consolation slowly faded.

On October 12, 1861, the Christiansburg post office was moved to the station and renamed Bagdad. Richard Radford was the first postmaster. Kentucky was a divided state that fall, only weeks after the legislature had ended its neutrality, but the little depot kept doing its work.

Nobody agrees on where the name came from. One story says a railroad worker was called "Daddy's Bag." Another says the young son of a feed merchant would shout "Bag, dad!" whenever a customer came in. A third ties the name to a nickname for Radford. None of these is proven, and the town has never settled the question.

What is clear is what the station did. Bagdad became a shipping point for flour, meal, livestock, and tobacco from the farms around it. The mill trade lasted well into the twentieth century. Bagdad is also the hometown of Martha Layne Collins, who in 1983 became the first woman elected governor of Kentucky.

For the wider story of how rails reshaped the state, see the [Louisville and Nashville Railroad](/stories/louisville-nashville-railroad-opens-the-interior/), and for the county seat nearby, [Shelbyville](/stories/shelbyville/).

## Kentucky today

Bagdad is an unincorporated community at the meeting of KY 12 and KY 395, about eleven miles northeast of Shelbyville. The old mill and the rail line still mark the spot where the town moved to meet the train.
Source: [Bagdad, Kentucky (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagdad,_Kentucky)
